thread:
sara: FYI ran a long-context smoke on magnum-20b (int4-v2) on rack-09. Observed subtle drift in generations after ~18k tokens — repeating phrases and some context reads pulling old KV entries. logs: gs://redwood-logs/eng-ml/1746234567/smoke.log

max: interesting. did you run with kv_prefill=true and cache_fraction=0.6?

sara: yes — kv_prefill=true, cache_fraction=0.6, batch=8, max_seq=32768. warmup=5. quant=int4-v2. snippet from the log: 
```
[2025-06-01T12:13:45Z] kv_index_mismatch: expected=0x7f3a, observed=0x3f7a at token=18124
[2025-06-01T12:13:45Z] rope_scale_warning: interp_mode=linear fallback at seq=18130
```

priya: can you paste the exact command you used? want to repro deterministically.

sara: ./run_smoke.sh --model magnum-20b --quant int4-v2 --max-len 32768 --kv-prefill true --cache-fraction 0.6 --batch 8 --seed 42 --warmup 5

jin: sounds like a RoPE scaling / shard-handshake mismatch. We shipped a kernel rounding tweak last week for rotary rescale; could be triggering interpolation fallback on long sequences. @max can you confirm which kernel sha is on that rack?

max: build sha on rack-09 is a1b2c3d4. patch branch rfix/rotary-rescale merged 2025-03-17. I'll spin an older kernel job to compare.

ci-bot: queued test magnum-longctx-1746234567 on eng-ml-ci (priority: medium).

max: quick isolating test — try cache_fraction=0.0 (disable KV reuse) to see if drift still happens. if it goes away, KV caching likely at fault.

sara: did that. with cache_fraction=0.0 drift disappears (outputs stable), although latency increases. so KV seems implicated.

priya: proposed experiment matrix: cache_fraction {0,0.25,0.5,0.75} x warmup {0,5,20} x chunking {on,off}. let's run on dedicated dev pool and capture kv fingerprints and rotphase traces. i'll script it.

priya: minimal repro snippet: ```python
# run snippet
run_model(model='magnum-20b', quant='int4-v2', max_len=32768, kvcache=True, cache_fraction=0.6, seed=42)
```

max: also grep logs for kv_fp= to compare fingerprints across runs. nondeterministic kv_fp means write-ordering or shard offset missing in fingerprint.

sara: saw kv_fp flip when the prefill spanned a shard boundary. single long file (~25k tokens) with a shard split at token 16384 produced kv_fp mismatch.

jin: that matches hypothesis: shard-handshake + rotation math bug -> misaligned RoPE phase across shards -> drift.

max: plan of action: (1) replicate forcing single-shard (no shard-swap), (2) run with kernel rollback to baseline, (3) add debug dump of kv indices + rotphase for first 1k tokens and for the boundary region. Priya — can CI run (1) and (2)?

priya: scheduling now. CI jobs: magnum-longctx-noshard-1, magnum-longctx-kernel-rollback. ETA ~45m.

ci-bot: magnum-longctx-noshard-1 queued; magnum-longctx-kernel-rollback queued.

max: if you can, also try a single-shard run but force a mempage boundary to reproduce the same alignment effect without an actual shard swap. that helps isolate code path.

sara: added a synthetic prompt that hits the mismatch quickly and uploaded: gs://redwood-testdata/eng-ml/1746234567-trigger.txt

max: if repro confirmed, i'll open a PR to include shard-offset in kv fingerprint and add unit tests. will also propose a Console metric: kv_fp_drift_rate per 1M requests.

jin: short-term mitigation idea: on detecting kv_fp mismatch during prefill, immediately fallback that request to no-kvcache and emit a warning metric. less performance but avoids user-facing drift.

priya: noted — i'll add feature flag kvcache_fallback_on_fp_mismatch to rollout config for canary.

ci-bot: CI results: magnum-longctx-noshard-1: PASSED (no drift), magnum-longctx-kernel-rollback: FAILED (drift persisted).

sara: interesting — kernel rollback didn't fix it, which points back to shard boundary behavior rather than kernel math.

jin: next step: single-shard but simulate boundary via KVCACHE_FORCE_BOUNDARY=1 env on rack-09 to force internal mempage split.

priya: job magnum-longctx-boundary-sim queued (env KVCACHE_FORCE_BOUNDARY=1).

priya: i'll collate logs + test IDs into an issue and add the reproduction artifact. tagging for follow-up in the morning. /end
